newsitem.title: USA: Jury reaches decision in Du Pont murder trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury reaches decision in Du Pont murder trial.

text.p: A Pennsylvania jury has reached a verdict in the murder trial of millionaire chemicals heir John du Pont, accused in the January, 1996, killing of Olympic champion wrestler David Schultz, du Pont's attorney said Tuesday.
Thomas Bergstrom told Reuters the verdict would be delivered at about 5 p.m. EST in the courtroom at Delaware County Court of Common Pleas.
The jury of six men and six women has been deliberating since Feb. 18.

Lawyers for du Pont, 58, had acknowledged he killed Schultz at the wrestler's home on the du Pont estate, but sought a verdict of not-guilty by reason of insanity, arguing du Pont suffered from paranoid schizophrenia that rendered him incapable of knowing right from wrong.
Prosecutors agreed du Pont was mentally ill, but said he knew killing Schultz was wrong and acted out of anger and resentment over Schultz's popularity in the wrestling world.

Du Pont, a fan and patron of amateur wrestling, established training facility on his estate. Schultz worked as a coach at the facility and lived with his wife and two young children in a house on the estate.
